prompt: Candid documentary photo of a real serving of gado-gado as eaten at a small Padang-style warung in Jakarta: a mound of blanched and steamed vegetables (long beans, bean sprouts, cabbage, kangkung water spinach, bitter melon, cassava leaves), cubes of fried tofu and tempeh, slices of compressed rice cake (lontong), and a halved boiled egg, all heavily smothered in a thick, warm, pale-brown peanut sauce (from ground peanuts, palm sugar, tamarind, chili, garlic) poured over everything so the vegetables are barely visible under the sauce. Two or three krupuk udang (prawn crackers) leaning on the plate. Served on a chipped plain white plate or banana leaf, on a worn wooden or formica warung table, a glass of iced tea (es teh manis) and a small sambal jar softly out of focus behind. Soft natural daylight from the open shopfront, viewed from about 40 degrees above, 35mm lens, moderate depth of field. Everyday unstyled plating, slightly messy edges with sauce pooling and drips, true-to-life colours, realistic textures. No food styling, no non-traditional garnish, no microgreens, no studio lighting, no text, no logos, no people, no hands.
